Stop signs used to be yellow. And their shape is a ranking.
In the 1920s, engineers made a rule: the more sides a sign has, the more dangerous the spot.
Rectangles just gave directions. Diamonds said: careful.
The circle, with endless sides, got the scariest job: railroad crossings.
Eight sides came next. The octagon got: stop.
But it was stuck in yellow. Red paint faded in the sun.
The circle's sign is still yellow today. And almost nobody remembers...
